newsitem.title: USA: U.S. corp bond issuance to continue at steady pace.
newsitem.headline: U.S. corp bond issuance to continue at steady pace.

text.p: With U.S. Treasury yields at their lowest levels since early spring, corporations are expected to wrap up their financing needs in the next two weeks, dealers said.
"It's still a very attractive market," said one syndicate source. "I imagine this week and next week would be the time to issue debt as everyone is still around."
With holidays and the year's end on the horizon, many issuers are expected to bring debt to market now when they can meet with full market reception.
"As we get closer to the holidays, it's difficult to structure these deals when desks become thinly staffed," said one dealer.
Goodyear is expected to issue $250 million in 10-year debt via lead underwriter Chase Securities. Price talk on the issue is in the area of 65 basis points over U.S. Treasuries.
The Republic of Italy is expected to issue a $1.0 billion in 10-year global deal. Price talk is seen between 40 and 45 basis points over Treasuries, sources said.
Union Central Life is expected to tap the market with a $500 million two-part debt offering, sources said.
Also, Western Mining is expected to price $250 million in 10 and 30-year noncallable debt via Merrill Lynch & Co.
In addition, Stuart Entertainment is expected to issue $100 million in seven-year debt.
Meanwhile, the recent onslaught of preferred issues is expected to continue into the last few weeks of the year as they continue to meet with good reception, dealers said.

"For the last week and a half there was a bunch of preferred deals every day...they're the hot topic," said one syndicate source. "I don't have any names or dates but more are expected to hit the market."
Turning to the high-yield primary sector, a slew of new issues are lining up to come to market, dealers said.
AK Steel Corp is getting set to bring $550 million in 10-year 144A senior notes via CS First Boston in the next few weeks, dealers said.
AES China Generating Co is expected to set a $150 million 10-year senior note offering via Morgan Stanley & Co Inc.
Also, Building Materials Corp is expected to issue $100 million in 144A 10-year senior notes via Bear Stearns.
Phonetel Tech is expected to issue $110 million in senior notes due 2006 via JP Morgan Securities.
Jacor Communications is expected to issue $125 million in 10-year senior subordinated notes via Donaldson Lufkin & Jenrette.
Quest Diagnostics is expected to issue $150 million in senior subordinated notes due 2006 via JP Morgan Securities.
Delta Beverage Group is also expected to issue $120 million in seven-year 144A notes via Nationsbanc Capital markets.
In the government market, the 30-year U.S. Treasury bond is off 8/32 at 101-20/32 to yield 6.38 percent.
--Nancy Leinfuss, 212-859-1675
